result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d erase the illusion of separation—the idea that we are anything less than deeply, inextricably connected. Not just to each other, but to the earth, to the air, to the stranger on the street, to the animals we share this planet with, even to the pain and joy that move through us like the same storm.

I’d make it impossible to forget that every act of cruelty, every act of kindness, every indifference, every choice—ripples outward in ways we can’t always see. Not as guilt, but as clarity. So that harming another would feel like harming yourself, and lifting another would feel like rising with them.

It wouldn’t fix everything. But it might make us pause. And in that pause, the world might begin to change itself.
